angle-3.label: Infrastructure Betrayal

angle-3.label: One Quarter Behind

angle-1.label: Growth Exposes You
angle-1.expansion: You built a system that worked — until the company succeeded. Now the thing you own is the reason scale feels impossible.

angle-1.label: You're the Ceiling
angle-1.expansion: Leadership sees a scaling org. They don't see that your comp infrastructure has already hit its limit. When it breaks publicly, that gap becomes yours to explain.

angle-1.label: Behind Before You Start

angle-2.label: The Tool Outgrew You First

angle-2.label: Growth Becomes the Risk

angle-2.label: The Urgency Isn't Yours to Control

angle-1.label: Single Point of Failure
angle-1.expansion: Your entire commission operation lives in one person's head and one file on their desktop. The day they're out sick, you find out exactly how fragile your infrastructure is.

angle-1.label: Ops Ceiling Is Growth Ceiling
angle-1.expansion: You're not running a scalable comp function — you're running a person at capacity. Every new rep, every new plan, every mid-year change hits the same single lane.

angle-1.label: Invisible Until It Breaks

angle-2.label: You Sign Off on the Mistake

angle-3.label: Human Failover Risk

angle-3.label: Strategy Held Hostage

angle-1.label: Key Person Hostage

angle-1.label: No Handoff, No Safety Net
angle-1.expansion: If they leave tomorrow, you can't explain how the numbers were built. You're not running comp ops — you're hoping nothing changes.

angle-2.label: Knowledge Held Hostage

angle-2.label: Continuity Is Your Job
angle-2.expansion: When comp breaks mid-cycle because no one can decode the formula, that's not a spreadsheet failure — that's you failing to build a system that outlasts any one person.

angle-1.label: You Become the Error

angle-1.label: Invisible Tax on Credibility
angle-1.expansion: You built the process, so every reconciliation hour and rep complaint is a quiet vote of no confidence in your ability to run the function.

angle-1.label: Trust You Can't Reclaim

angle-2.label: Recurring Doubt Tax
angle-2.expansion: Every cycle, you're not closing — you're re-opening. The model you built is never fully trusted, and that distrust lands on you.

angle-2.label: Builder Becomes Debugger
angle-2.expansion: You were hired to design systems that run. Instead you spend close week hunting down why a formula broke on a rep who split territory mid-quarter.

angle-2.label: Edge Case Owns You
angle-2.expansion: The one scenario you didn't model becomes the one everyone remembers. Your entire system gets judged by the exception, not the rule.

angle-3.label: Single Point of Failure

angle-3.label: Invisible Until It's Wrong

angle-3.label: The Ownership Trap

angle-1.label: The Pre-Run Ritual Tax

angle-1.label: The System Owns Your Calendar
angle-1.expansion: You didn't sign up to be a data janitor. But three sources that don't talk to each other means every close cycle is yours to manually stitch together before anyone else can move.

angle-1.label: Single Point of Failure

angle-2.label: Coordination Tax

angle-2.label: Fragility Owns You

angle-2.label: Invisible Dependency Risk
angle-2.expansion: The moment a handoff fails silently, you're the one presenting numbers you can't fully stand behind. The error isn't yours — but your name is on the output.

angle-2.label: Ritual Without Return

angle-2.label: Expertise Laundered Into Drudgery
angle-2.expansion: You were hired to design systems that scale. Instead, you're the system — the manual step no one automated because it was easier to rely on you.

angle-1.label: Doing Work Below Your Level

angle-1.label: Firefighting Crowds Out Building

angle-1.label: Hard to Champion What Hasn't Shipped

angle-1.label: You Own the Delay

angle-1.label: Authority Without Infrastructure

angle-2.label: Held Hostage by the Process

angle-1.label: Single Point of Failure

angle-2.label: You Are the System

angle-2.label: Unauditable Authority

angle-2.label: Credibility Lag
